categories.answer: Buses are getting more expensive, in special education and in the regular-route contract. The state repays only a slice of special education busing. The athletic line rose because the district moved that cost from player fees to the town budget, mostly taxes.
categories.title: School bus costs

categories.answer: Athletics is paid from two pots, the town budget and a fee fund. The town’s ledger shows $439,510 paid in FY2026 and the fee fund $146,911; the district’s own sheets disagree on what each team costs, by a multiple.
categories.title: Athletics costs

categories.answer: Out-of-district tuition was $1,205,949 in FY2025, and 39.3% of it was paid outside the general fund. The state repaid $579,142 in FY2026 through the circuit breaker, a year after the costs.
categories.title: Special education costs

categories.answer: The town keeps two kinds of reserve: free cash, $3,354,370 as of 1 July 2025, and nine stabilization accounts holding $9,061,421. Only the general fund’s $3,147,179 may be spent on anything lawful.
categories.title: Free cash and stabilization

categories.answer: The school general fund closed FY2026 with $482,118 unspent, 1.8% of its budget, at period 13. Town departments stood $858,462 under in June, before their close.
categories.title: FY2026 year end

athletic-bus-funding.finding: From FY2025, athletic buses moved from player fees to the town budget, mostly taxes.
athletic-bus-funding.title: Athletic bus funding

athletic-fee.finding: The high school fee for a first child, a season, went from $250 in FY2025 to $325 in FY2026.
athletic-fee.title: Athletic fee

away-trips-by-sport.finding: The posted schedules list 240 away games in FY2026, about 176 bus trips by our estimate.
away-trips-by-sport.title: Away trips by sport

bus-cost-by-sport.finding: Track costs most on the district’s sheet: $13,864 in FY2024, ahead of the next sport’s $9,078.
bus-cost-by-sport.title: Bus cost by sport

bus-fee.finding: The new bus fee did not lower what the school budget paid for buses in FY2026.
bus-fee.title: Bus fee

circuit-breaker.finding: The state paid $579,142 in FY2026 on $1,257,225 of eligible costs for 9 children: 46.1%.
circuit-breaker.title: Circuit breaker

circuit-breaker-account.finding: The account closed FY2026 at $281,806, down from $482,004 at the close of FY2020.
circuit-breaker-account.title: Circuit breaker account

class-size-limits.finding: A separate special education group may hold 8 students to one educator, or 12 with an aide.
class-size-limits.title: Class size limits

cost-per-placement.finding: No published document says what one out-of-district placement costs.
cost-per-placement.title: Cost per placement

cost-per-sport.finding: Not one of 25 teams carries the same FY2024 cost in all three district sheets.
cost-per-sport.title: Cost per sport

dee-bus-contract.finding: Regular routes cost exactly the contract price, which is fixed through FY2028.
dee-bus-contract.title: Dee Bus contract

fee-fund-ledger.finding: The fee fund’s cash fell $103,853 in FY2024; four journal entries then brought in $254,121 in FY2025.
fee-fund-ledger.title: Fee fund ledger

free-cash-and-capital.finding: Free cash paid $655,424 of the $1,225,000 FY2026 capital programme; FY2027 plans $991,627 of $1,830,203.
free-cash-and-capital.title: Free cash and capital

free-cash-balance.finding: The state certified $3,354,370 of free cash as of 1 July 2025, the most in any year the Town’s records list.
free-cash-balance.title: Free cash balance

free-cash-guideline.finding: Free cash is 6.65% of the budget, inside the 5% to 7% the Town cites; 7 of the last 10 years fell short.
free-cash-guideline.title: Free cash guideline

free-cash-redirect.finding: Kept above the 5% floor, $794,872 could be redirected, $135,401 short of the FY2028 gap (our arithmetic).
free-cash-redirect.title: Free cash for schools

free-cash-sources.finding: Two thirds of the free cash identified in July 2025, $2,457,761, was money appropriated and not spent.
free-cash-sources.title: Free cash sources

fy2025-school-surplus.finding: FY2025 closed with $627,117 unspent, $23,231 more than the figure the School Committee was given.
fy2025-school-surplus.title: FY2025 school surplus

fy2026-athletics-underspend.finding: Athletics closed FY2026 with $55,300 of its $518,334 town budget unspent, on the town’s ledger.
fy2026-athletics-underspend.title: FY2026 athletics underspend

fy2026-lines-over-budget.finding: 57 school accounts closed FY2026 past their budgets; in FY2025, 4 did.
fy2026-lines-over-budget.title: Lines over budget

fy2026-paraprofessional-overrun.finding: Paraprofessional accounts ran $208,082 over in FY2026; $99,064 of it was paid against no budget.
fy2026-paraprofessional-overrun.title: Paraprofessional overrun

fy2026-psychologist-line.finding: One of four school psychologist accounts, $98,784 budgeted, paid nothing in FY2026.
fy2026-psychologist-line.title: Psychologist line

fy2026-school-retiree-insurance.finding: An account named for school retiree health paid $1,262,376 from the town’s insurance department.
fy2026-school-retiree-insurance.title: School retiree insurance

fy2026-school-surplus.finding: The school general fund closed FY2026 with $482,118 unspent and uncommitted, 1.8% of its budget.
fy2026-school-surplus.title: FY2026 school surplus

fy2026-school-transfers.finding: Transfers moved $394,929 into school accounts and $309,839 out; the department ended $85,090 up, net.
fy2026-school-transfers.title: Year-end transfers

fy2026-snow-and-reserve-fund.finding: Snow removal paid $1,038,092 against $355,571 voted; the $185,000 Reserve Fund paid nothing.
fy2026-snow-and-reserve-fund.title: Snow and Reserve Fund

fy2026-surplus-and-fy2027.finding: The FY2027 school budget was set $761,000 below level service; FY2026 then closed $482,118 unspent.
fy2026-surplus-and-fy2027.title: Surplus and FY2027 budget

fy2026-surplus-by-category.finding: Accounts under budget left $1,683,552 and accounts over used $1,201,434 of it; the net is $482,118.
fy2026-surplus-by-category.title: Surplus by category

fy2026-town-unspent.finding: In June, before the close, town departments stood $858,462 under a $27,647,670 budget.
fy2026-town-unspent.title: Town unspent balance

fy2026-tuition-lines.finding: FY2027 budgets $700,142 for the two tuition lines on which FY2026 spent $1,202,771.
fy2026-tuition-lines.title: Tuition at year end

fy2027-athletic-bus-cut.finding: FY2027 cut athletic buses from the town budget, then put $60,000 back, most on the fee fund.
fy2027-athletic-bus-cut.title: FY2027 athletic bus cut

fy2027-bus-budget.finding: School-day buses rise 11.2% in FY2027; the total shows 2.4% because athletic buses were cut.
fy2027-bus-budget.title: FY2027 bus budget

general-stabilization-fund.finding: The general fund’s cash rose every year from FY2012 to FY2025, to $3,147,179.
general-stabilization-fund.title: General stabilization fund

hiring-versus-placing.finding: Placements fell while in-district budgets rose; nothing published shows one caused the other.
hiring-versus-placing.title: Hiring versus placing

in-district-special-education.finding: The paraprofessional budget line grew 12.78% a year over 10 budgets; the state’s FTE fell 63.3%.
in-district-special-education.title: In-district special education

out-of-district-placements.finding: The town counted 10 children placed out of district in FY2025, against 30 in FY2015.
out-of-district-placements.title: Out-of-district placements

out-of-district-tuition.finding: $1,205,949 went to out-of-district tuition in FY2025; 39.3% of it was paid outside the general fund.
out-of-district-tuition.title: Out-of-district tuition

participation.finding: The district counted 649 sport participations in FY2026, against 675 in FY2024.
participation.title: Participation

reserves-and-the-gap.finding: Spent on the school gap, the general fund covers FY2028 and FY2029 and runs out in FY2030, by our arithmetic.
reserves-and-the-gap.title: Reserves against the gap

special-education-overruns.finding: In the worst of 17 years, FY2013, special education needed $223,774 beyond its voted budget.
special-education-overruns.title: Special education overruns

special-education-transportation.finding: The fastest-growing bus line: 10.1% a year, and $67,555 past its FY2026 budget.
special-education-transportation.title: Special education transportation

spending-by-category.finding: Coaches and buses cost most on the district’s sheet; the town’s officials account held $0 in FY2026.
spending-by-category.title: Spending by category

stabilization-balances.finding: The town’s ledger files $9,061,421 under its nine stabilization accounts, at the start of FY2026.
stabilization-balances.title: Stabilization fund balances

stabilization-deposits.finding: Town Meeting put $350,000 into the two town funds in May 2024, and passed over both articles in May 2025.
stabilization-deposits.title: Stabilization deposits

stabilization-withdrawals.finding: The record shows $317,392 taken from stabilization funds in 9 votes, none from the general fund.
stabilization-withdrawals.title: Stabilization withdrawals

state-reimbursement.finding: The state repays 5.5% of what the town spends on buses, all of it for special education.
state-reimbursement.title: State reimbursement

students-with-an-iep.finding: 258 Lunenburg children had a special education plan in FY2026, 16.3% of those enrolled.
students-with-an-iep.title: Students with an IEP

total-athletics-cost.finding: No document states one total: three sheets give $185,356 to $349,145 for the same teams in FY2024.
total-athletics-cost.title: Total athletics cost

town-budget-and-fee-fund.finding: The fee fund paid 45.8% of athletics spending in FY2024 and 5.7% in FY2025, on the town’s books.
town-budget-and-fee-fund.title: Town budget and fee fund

tuition-budget.finding: FY2027 budgets out-of-district tuition at $700,142, $591,151 below FY2026, a 46% cut.
tuition-budget.title: Tuition budget

who-may-spend-it.finding: Only the general fund, $3,147,179 of $9,061,421, may go to any lawful use, by a two-thirds vote.
who-may-spend-it.title: Who may spend it
